name: Evidence Action's Dispensers for Safe Water (The Life You Can Save, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: The locations the sheet's bottom line reads (row labels naming Kenya, Uganda, Malawi), sharing equally.

missing_data.note: Measured: Evidence Action counts the dispensers installed and the people with access in each country, and its deaths and cases averted apply the effect of water chlorination from randomised trials to those children.

summary: Evidence Action installs chlorine dispensers at village water points in Kenya, Uganda and Malawi so families can treat their drinking water. The Life You Can Save turns Evidence Action's 2024 estimates of children's deaths and diarrhoea cases averted into DALYs and divides by the programme's 2024 cost in each country. Our view values the deaths the site's way and adds the benefits the sheet leaves out (older people's health, later earnings, treatment costs); the biggest uncertainties are Evidence Action's own estimates of deaths averted, still under review for Uganda and Malawi.

Value of averting a child's death, in healthy years
rows.explainer: **Changed for consistency.** The Life You Can Save counts a child's death averted as the remaining life expectancy at age 2.5, discounted at 3% (28.6 to 28.8 years). The site values every child's death the same way: GiveWell's moral weight for a death under five times the value-of-a-life slider, in healthy years at Your values' exchange rate.

rows.label: Share of the deaths and cases averted that wouldn't have been without Evidence Action
rows.explainer: ×1, our judgment: Evidence Action's figures are already its marginal impact, against the disease burden without the dispensers, and nobody else would chlorinate these water points.

rows.label: Later earnings of children kept healthy, as a share of the deaths' value
rows.explainer:
The sheet counts only health. Children spared diarrhoea grow and learn better and earn more as adults; the site's shared figure (GiveWell's long-term income gains as a share of the value of the deaths averted).

Changed for consistency: GiveWell's ratio is at its own values (income from 10 years on, discounted at 4%, valued at 1/ln 2, against its weight on a death). Like every other model that reads it, ours rescales it: the present value of those 40 years at your discount rate over the same at 4%, times the income slider over 1/ln 2, divided by the weight on a life. At the defaults it is GiveWell's ratio.

rows.label: Health of people aged five and over, as a share of the children's
rows.explainer: Everyone drinking from the water point is protected, but the sheet counts only children under five, whose deaths are most of diarrhoea's burden. Our judgment, 10% (0 to 30%).

rows.label: Treatment costs households and clinics are spared, as a share of the health value
rows.explainer: Fewer cases mean less spent on treatment (Evidence Action's monitoring puts the medical costs averted at about $5 million in 2024). The site's shared figure, GiveWell's supplemental adjustment.

rows.label: Our healthy years for the same work, as a share of The Life You Can Save's DALYs
rows.formula: (deaths_total * healthy_years_per_death * (1 + income_share + over_five_share) + yld_total) * counterfactual_share * (1 + treatment_costs_share) / dalys_total
rows.explainer: The evaluator view keeps The Life You Can Save's (1).

rows.label: Evidence Action's spending beyond the country costs, per dollar of them
rows.explainer: The country costs are those billed to the programme; Evidence Action's headquarters, management and fundraising come on top. Our judgment, 10% (0 to 20%).

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of programme cost
rows.explainer: Default for programmes that mostly buy and hand out goods: dispensers and chlorine, kept filled by local promoters. Our judgment.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Promoters and field staff are hired locally. Our judgment.
